Consider the picture above. Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda \mathbf{a}+\mu \mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda $ and $\mu .$
solution:
![](images/60/601e049067de307ef2321ae9b516d1c7306d837ca0758c080074446a8c54389d.png)

In $△OAC$ shown above, we have:

- $OA=2|\mathbf{a}|$

- $\overset{\to }{OA}$ and $\mathbf{a}$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OA}=2\mathbf{a}.$

Similarly:

- $AC=2|\mathbf{b}|$

- $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{AC}=2\mathbf{b}.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{c} & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AC} \\  & =2\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $\mathbf{c}=\lambda \mathbf{a}+\mu \mathbf{b}=2\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.$ 

Since $\mathbf{a}∦\mathbf{b},$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =2$ and $\mu =2$
